A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEMERAG study. Their complete text, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original human-annotation results, inter-annotator agreement and LLM-as-judge experiments, including extended-dataset and fine-grained analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original annotation outcomes and evaluator experiments, including Tables 2–13 and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The question filtering, context selection, answer generation, annotation workflow and automatic-evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Moving generator names from a footnote into Section 3.3 does not introduce different models or methods.

E1.justification: Both versions cover English, German, Spanish, French and Hindi, with the same faithfulness and relevance tasks. MEMERAG-Ext already appears in v3 Appendix B; its new main-text mention does not add dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4o mini, Qwen 2.5 32B and Llama 3.2 11B/90B, evaluated with ZS, COT, AG and AG+COT prompts. Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 5 and the appendix results.

E3.justification: Filtering, sample sizes, annotation assignments, label exclusions and evaluator retry settings remain unchanged. Section 5.1 retains balanced accuracy with equal weighting across labels and languages; removing its explanatory appendix does not change the metric.

E4.justification: The annotation-pilot investigations, extended-dataset agreement analysis, English error heatmaps in Figure 5 and French fine-grained analysis in Table 13 are retained. The latter moves from Appendix J to Appendix I without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions retain permutation testing at alpha = 0.05 in Appendix E and standard errors calculated using 1,000 bootstrap iterations in Tables 10–11. The five-annotator information highlighted in v4 was already documented in v3 Appendix B.

E6.justification: All 13 tables retain identical data, and the figures and reported findings are unchanged. Section 4 switches its Spanish–English verbosity comparison from 563 versus 400 sentences to 52.1 versus 30.3 words; both pairs already appear in Table 1 in both versions.

T1.justification: v4 removes v3 Appendix F, which explains the standard binary balanced-accuracy formula and confusion-matrix terms. This is removal of explanatory material, without a change to mathematical reasoning, formal properties or the metric itself.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list are unchanged. Claims concerning the native multilingual benchmark, annotation quality and usefulness for prompt selection, model selection and fine-grained analysis retain the same scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of language differences, annotation subjectivity, prompt effects and evaluator errors are retained. Section 7 preserves the same limitations, and Section 4 still attributes Spanish relevance-label differences partly to verbosity.

D1.justification: Generation settings, preprocessing, annotation guidance, complete prompt templates and dataset-release information remain available. The relocated generator list and added appendix pointers expose no previously undocumented implementation or access information.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. Citation-format edits do not alter the cited works, novelty claims or positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited wording edits, revises author and equal-contribution notes, corrects Table 1 references and highlights existing MEMERAG-Ext documentation. It removes the explanatory Balanced Accuracy appendix and renumbers subsequent appendices while preserving their order and content.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables retain their designs and structures, with modest layout changes. Tables 6–7 move from PDF page 13 to page 11, prompt boxes are rearranged, and printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: Correcting the dataset references to Table 1 and adding pointers to existing MEMERAG-Ext and prompt documentation modestly improve clarity. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. Removing the standard balanced-accuracy explanation reduces explanatory detail slightly, but Section 5.1 retains the metric and weighting.
